label: thmwellposedness
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thmwellposedness}
Let Assumptions (AOP) and (AG) hold and let \(\rho>-1\). For every initial data
\((u_0;u_1)\in\mathcal{H}_1\), Problem \eqref{abstract} admits a unique global solution
\(u\) on \([0,\infty)\). Moreover, this solution satisfies
\[
(u;u_t)\in L^{\infty}(0,\infty;\mathcal{H}_1),\qquad
u_{tt}\in L^{\infty}(0,\infty;V_0),
\]
and hence
\[
u\in C([0,\infty);V_1),\qquad u_t\in C([0,\infty);V_0).
\]
Consequently, \(u\) is a global solution in the sense of Definition~\ref{defweak}.

label: main
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{main}
Assume that (AOP) and (AG) hold, and let \(E(0)>0\).
\begin{enumerate}
\item For \(-1<\rho<0\),
\[
E(t)\leq C(\rho,\mu_0,\lambda_1,g(0),G_0,k)
\left(1+E(0)^{-\frac{\rho}{2\rho+2}}\right)^{\frac{2\rho+2}{|\rho|}}
t^{\frac{2\rho+2}{\rho}},\qquad t\geq t_0,
\]
where \(C(\rho,\mu_0,\lambda_1,g(0),G_0,k)>0\) is a constant depending only on the indicated parameters, and \(t_0>0\) is defined by
\[
\int_0^{t_0}g(s)ds=\frac12 G_0,
\]
with \(G_0=\int_0^\infty g(s)ds\) given in \eqref{G0}. Equivalently, since
\(-\frac{\rho}{2\rho+2}\in(0,\frac12)\) and
\(-\frac{2\rho+2}{\rho}=\frac{2\rho+2}{|\rho|}>0\), one may replace the
constant factor above by
\(\left(1+E(0)^{-1}\right)^{\frac{2\rho+2}{|\rho|}}\), at the cost of
enlarging the constant \(C\).

\item For \(\rho\geq0\), if the constant \(k\) in Assumption (AG) satisfies \(k\geq2g(0)\), then
\[
E(t)\leq
\begin{cases}
E(0)e^{-\kappa(t-1)^+}, & \rho=0,\\[1ex]
\left[\dfrac{\rho}{2\mu}(t-1)^++E(0)^{-\frac{\rho}{2}}\right]^{-\frac{2}{\rho}}, & \rho>0,
\end{cases}
\qquad t\geq0.
\]
Here
\[
\mu:=\left[2(E(0))^{\frac{\rho}{\rho+2}}+4\mu_1\right]^{1+\frac{\rho}{2}},\qquad
\kappa=-\log(1-1/\mu).
\]
Since \(\mu_1>0\) and \(\rho>0\), we have \(\mu>1\), so the constant
\(\kappa\) is well defined. Moreover,
\[
\mu_1:=\frac{32}{\mu_0\lambda_1}+\frac{4(2E(0))^\rho}{\mu_0\lambda_1}+\frac{3}{2}+\frac{2}{k}(E(0))^{\frac{\rho}{\rho+2}},
\]
with \(s^+:=\frac{1}{2}(s+|s|)\), and the positive constants \(\mu_0\) and \(\lambda_1\) given in \eqref{mu_0} and \eqref{lam}, respectively.
\end{enumerate}

title: Remark
body_md: The restriction \(\rho>-1\) is essential for the present approach. For \(\rho>-1\), the operator \(l(v)=\|v\|^\rho v\) is continuous, monotone, and semicontinuous on \(V_0\), and \(l(0)=0\). These properties are used both in the Faedo--Galerkin compactness argument and in the uniqueness proof. When \(\rho\le -1\), the operator \(l\) is no longer continuous and monotone at the origin; although the dissipation rate \(\|u_t\|^{\rho+2}\) remains nonnegative for \(\rho>-2\), the well-posedness theory requires a different approach. We therefore leave the case \(\rho\le -1\) for future work.

title: Proof
body_md:
If \(u=0\), then
\[
(l(u)-l(v),u-v)=(-\|v\|^{\rho}v,-v)=\|v\|^{\rho+2}\ge0;
\]
if \(v=0\), then
\[
(l(u)-l(v),u-v)=(\|u\|^{\rho}u,u)=\|u\|^{\rho+2}\ge0.
\]
Hence assume \(u\neq0\) and \(v\neq0\). For \(u,v\in V_0\), we have
\begin{align*}
(l(u)-l(v),u-v)
&=(\|u\|^{\rho}u-\|v\|^{\rho}v,u-v)\\
&=\|u\|^{\rho}(\|u\|^2-(u,v))+\|v\|^{\rho}(\|v\|^2-(u,v))\\
&\geq\|u\|^{\rho+2}-\|u\|^{\rho+1}\|v\|+\|v\|^{\rho+2}-\|v\|^{\rho+1}\|u\|\\
&=(\|u\|-\|v\|)(\|u\|^{\rho+1}-\|v\|^{\rho+1}).
\end{align*}
Since \(\rho+1>0\), the function \(t\mapsto t^{\rho+1}\) is nondecreasing on \([0,\infty)\), and hence the last expression is nonnegative. This proves (i).

To prove (ii), fix \(u,v,w\in V_0\) and set
\[
\phi(\lambda):=(l(u+\lambda v),w)=\|u+\lambda v\|^{\rho}((u,w)+\lambda(v,w)),\qquad \lambda\in\mathbb{R}.
\]
If \(u=0\) and \(v=0\), then \(\phi\equiv0\). If \(u=0\) and \(v\neq0\), then
\[
\phi(\lambda)=|\lambda|^{\rho}\lambda\|v\|^{\rho}(v,w),
\]
which is continuous at \(\lambda=0\) because \(\rho>-1\) implies \(\rho+1>0\), and continuous elsewhere by the continuity of \(\lambda\mapsto|\lambda|^\rho\lambda\) on \(\mathbb{R}\setminus\{0\}\). If \(u\neq0\) and \(v=0\), then \(\phi\) is constant.

Finally, if \(u\neq0\) and \(v\neq0\), we distinguish two cases.

\medskip
\noindent\emph{Case 1: there exists \(\lambda_0\in\mathbb{R}\) such that \(u+\lambda_0 v=0\).}
Such a \(\lambda_0\) is unique. On \(\mathbb{R}\setminus\{\lambda_0\}\), the continuity of \(\phi\) follows from the continuity of \(\lambda\mapsto\|u+\lambda v\|\) and of \(t\mapsto t^\rho\) on \((0,\infty)\). At \(\lambda=\lambda_0\), we have \(u+\lambda_0 v=0\), hence \((u,w)+\lambda_0(v,w)=0\), and
\[
\phi(\lambda)=\|u+\lambda v\|^{\rho}((\lambda-\lambda_0)(v,w))
=|\lambda-\lambda_0|^{\rho}(\lambda-\lambda_0)\|v\|^{\rho}(v,w)\to0
\]
as \(\lambda\to\lambda_0\), since \(\rho+1>0\). Thus \(\phi\) is continuous at \(\lambda_0\) as well, hence on all of \(\mathbb{R}\).

\medskip
\noindent\emph{Case 2: no such \(\lambda_0\) exists.}
Then \(u+\lambda v\neq0\) for every \(\lambda\in\mathbb{R}\), so \(\|u+\lambda v\|>0\) for every \(\lambda\). The continuity of \(\phi\) on \(\mathbb{R}\) follows from the continuity of \(\lambda\mapsto\|u+\lambda v\|\) and of \(t\mapsto t^\rho\) on \((0,\infty)\).

Thus \(\phi\) is continuous in all cases. This proves (ii).

label: weak
title: Proof
body_md:
Let \(\{\omega_k\}_{k=1}^\infty\) be the orthonormal basis of \(V_0\) given in \eqref{basis}. For each \(n\in\mathbb{N}\), we consider the approximate problem
\begin{align}
\left(u_{tt}^n(t),\omega_k\right)&+\left(Au^n(t),\omega_k\right)\notag\\
&-\left(\int_{0}^{t}g(t-s)Au^n(s)ds,\omega_k\right)
+\|u_t^n(t)\|^{\rho}\left(u_t^n(t),\omega_k\right)=0,\quad t>0,\label{weak}
\end{align}
for \(k=1,\dots,n\), where
\begin{equation}\label{bc1}
u^n(t)=\sum_{j=1}^n c_{nj}(t)\omega_j,\qquad u^n(0)=u^{n}_0,\qquad u^n_t(0)=u^{n}_1,
\end{equation}
and
\begin{align}
\left(u^{n}_0;u^{n}_1\right)\rightarrow(u_0;u_1)\quad\text{strongly in }\mathcal{H}_1\text{ as }n\to\infty.\label{defineun}
\end{align}

Substituting \eqref{bc1} into \eqref{weak}, we obtain the system of ordinary differential equations
\begin{align}
c''_{nk}&+\sum_{j=1}^{n}(A^{\frac12}\omega_j,A^{\frac12}\omega_k)c_{nj}\notag\\
&-\sum_{j=1}^{n}\left(A^{\frac12}\omega_j,A^{\frac12}\omega_k\right)
\int_{0}^{t}g(t-s)c_{nj}(s)ds
+F_k\left(c'_{n1},\dots,c'_{nn}\right)=0,\label{withouttime}
\end{align}
where
\[
F_k(c'_{n1},\dots,c'_{nn})
:=
\begin{cases}
\left(\sum_{j=1}^n(c'_{nj})^2\right)^{\rho/2}c'_{nk}, & \sum_{j=1}^n(c'_{nj})^2\ne0,\\[1ex]
0, & \sum_{j=1}^n(c'_{nj})^2=0.
\end{cases}
\]
Since \(\rho>-1\), the map \((c'_{n1},\dots,c'_{nn})\mapsto F_k(c'_{n1},\dots,c'_{nn})\) is continuous: indeed, with \(r=(\sum_{j=1}^n(c'_{nj})^2)^{1/2}\), we have \(|F_k|\leq r^{\rho+1}\to0\) as \(r\to0\), because \(\rho+1>0\). Moreover, the memory term is linear and continuous in \(c_{nj}\). Hence the right-hand side of \eqref{withouttime} is continuous in \((c_{nj},c'_{nj})\), and by the Peano existence theorem there exists a local solution \(c_{nk}\in C^2([0,T_n])\), \(k=1,\dots,n\), for some \(T_n>0\).

We now derive uniform a priori estimates on \([0,T_n]\). Multiplying \eqref{weak} by \(c'_{nk}(t)\) and summing over \(k=1,\dots,n\), we obtain
\begin{align}
\frac12\frac{d}{dt}&\left(\left\|u_t^n(t)\right\|^2+\left\|A^{\frac12}u^n(t)\right\|^2\right)\notag\\
&-\left(\int_{0}^{t}g(t-s)A^{\frac12}u^n(s)ds,A^{\frac12}u_t^n(t)\right)
+\|u_t^n\|^{\rho+2}=0.\label{oneorder}
\end{align}
We use the standard identity for the memory term,
\begin{align}
&-\left(\int_{0}^{t}g(t-s)A^{\frac12}u^n(s)ds,A^{\frac12}u_t^n(t)\right)\notag\\
=&\frac12\frac{d}{dt}\int_{0}^{t}g(t-s)\left\|A^{\frac12}u^n(t)-A^{\frac12}u^n(s)\right\|^2ds
-\frac12\int_{0}^{t}g'(t-s)\left\|A^{\frac12}u^n(t)-A^{\frac12}u^n(s)\right\|^2ds\notag\\
&+\frac12g(t)\left\|A^{\frac12}u^n(t)\right\|^2
-\frac12\frac{d}{dt}\left(\int_{0}^{t}g(s)ds\left\|A^{\frac12}u^n(t)\right\|^2\right).\label{import}
\end{align}
Substituting \eqref{import} into \eqref{oneorder} and integrating from \(0\) to \(t\), we obtain
\begin{align}
E_n(t)+\int_{0}^{t}\left\|u_t^n(s)\right\|^{\rho+2}ds=&E_n(0)+\frac12\int_{0}^{t}\int_{0}^{s}g'(s-\tau)\left\|A^{\frac12}u^n(s)-A^{\frac12}u^n(\tau)\right\|^2d\tau ds\notag\\
&-\frac12\int_{0}^{t}g(s)\left\|A^{\frac12}u^n(s)\right\|^2ds,\label{energyidentity}
\end{align}
where
\begin{align}
E_n(t):=&\frac12\left\|u_t^n(t)\right\|^2
+\frac12\left(1-\int_{0}^{t}g(s)ds\right)\left\|A^{\frac12}u^n(t)\right\|^2\notag\\
&+\frac12\int_{0}^{t}g(t-s)\left\|A^{\frac12}u^n(t)-A^{\frac12}u^n(s)\right\|^2ds.\label{En}
\end{align}
Since
\[
E_n(0)=\frac12\left(\|u_1^n\|^2+\left\|A^{\frac12}u_0^n\right\|^2\right)
\le C\left(\|(u_0^n;u_1^n)\|_{\mathcal{H}_1}\right),
\]
and \((u_0^n;u_1^n)\) is uniformly bounded in \(\mathcal{H}_1\) by \eqref{defineun}, the term \(E_n(0)\) is uniformly bounded. Since \(g'\leq0\) and \(g\geq0\), the last two terms on the right-hand side of \eqref{energyidentity} are nonpositive. Hence, by \eqref{mu_0},
\begin{align}\label{weakestimateone}
\left\|u_t^n(t)\right\|^2&+\left\|A^{\frac12}u^n(t)\right\|^2\notag\\
&+\int_0^t g(t-s)\left\|A^{\frac12}u^n(t)-A^{\frac12}u^n(s)\right\|^2ds
\leq C\left(\|(u_0;u_1)\|_{\mathcal{H}_1}\right),
\end{align}
for all \(t\in[0,T_n]\). In particular, by \eqref{defineun},
\begin{equation}\label{weakestimateoneb}
\left\|u_t^n(t)\right\|^2+\left\|A^{\frac12}u^n(t)\right\|^2\leq C\left(\|(u_0;u_1)\|_{\mathcal{H}_1}\right),\qquad t\in[0,T_n].
\end{equation}

Next, multiplying \eqref{weak} by \(\lambda_kc'_{nk}(t)\) and summing over \(k=1,\dots,n\), we obtain
\begin{align*}
\frac12\frac{d}{dt}&\left(\left\|A^{\frac12}u_t^n(t)\right\|^2+\left\|Au^n(t)\right\|^2\right)
\\
&-\left(\int_{0}^{t}g(t-s)Au^n(s)ds,Au_t^n(t)\right)
+\|u_t^n\|^{\rho}\left\|A^{\frac12}u^n_t\right\|^2=0.
\end{align*}
Using the same identity for the memory term with \(A^{1/2}u^n\) replaced by \(Au^n\), and noting that \(\|u_t^n\|^{\rho}\|A^{1/2}u_t^n\|^2\geq0\), we deduce
\begin{align}
\left\|A^{\frac12}u_t^n(t)\right\|^2+\left\|Au^n(t)\right\|^2\leq C\left(\|(u_0;u_1)\|_{\mathcal{H}_1}\right),\qquad t\in[0,T_n].\label{weaktwo}
\end{align}

Finally, multiplying \eqref{weak} by \(c''_{nk}(t)\) and summing over \(k=1,\dots,n\), we get
\[
\|u_{tt}^n\|^2=\sum_{i=1}^{3}Y_i,
\]
where
\[
Y_1:=-\left(Au^n(t),u_{tt}^n\right),\quad
Y_2:=\left(\int_{0}^{t}g(t-s)Au^n(s)ds,u_{tt}^n\right),\quad
Y_3:=-\|u_t^n\|^{\rho}\left(u_t^n,u_{tt}^n\right).
\]
By Cauchy's inequality, Young's inequality, \eqref{mu_0}, \eqref{G0}, \eqref{weakestimateoneb} and \eqref{weaktwo}, we obtain
\[
|Y_1|\leq\frac16\left\|u_{tt}^n\right\|^2+C\left(\|(u_0;u_1)\|_{\mathcal{H}_1}\right),
\]
\[
|Y_2|\leq\frac16\left\|u_{tt}^n\right\|^2+C\left(\|(u_0;u_1)\|_{\mathcal{H}_1}\right),
\]
\[
|Y_3|\leq\frac16\left\|u_{tt}^n\right\|^2+C\left(\|(u_0;u_1)\|_{\mathcal{H}_1}\right).
\]
Indeed, for \(Y_2\) we used
\[
\left\|\int_0^t g(t-s)Au^n(s)ds\right\|
\leq G_0\|Au^n\|_{L^\infty(0,\infty;V_0)}\leq C,
\]
and for \(Y_3\) we used \(\|u_t^n\|\leq C\) together with the fact that,
since \(\rho+1>0\), the function \(s\mapsto s^{\rho+1}\) is continuous on
\([0,\infty)\) and hence bounded on \([0,C]\), which gives
\(\|u_t^n\|^{\rho+1}\leq C\). Hence
\begin{align}
\|u_{tt}^n\|^2\leq C(\|(u_0;u_1)\|_{\mathcal{H}_1}),\qquad t\in[0,T_n].\label{utt}
\end{align}
Combining \eqref{defineun}, \eqref{weakestimateoneb}, \eqref{weaktwo} and \eqref{utt}, we arrive at
\begin{equation}\label{bc8}
\|u_{t}^n(t)\|^2+\|u_{tt}^n(t)\|^2+\left\|A^{\frac12}u_t^n(t)\right\|^2+\left\|Au^n(t)\right\|^2\leq C\left(\|(u_0;u_1)\|_{\mathcal{H}_1}\right),\quad t\in[0,T_n].
\end{equation}
Since the bound on the right-hand side of \eqref{bc8} is independent of \(T_n\), the local solution can be extended to all \(t\geq0\), and hence \(T_n=\infty\). Consequently, the estimates \eqref{weakestimateoneb}, \eqref{weaktwo}, \eqref{utt} and \eqref{bc8} hold for all \(t\in[0,\infty)\).

From \eqref{bc8}, \eqref{G0} and \(\rho>-1\), we further obtain, for all \(t\in[0,\infty)\),
\[
\left\|\|u_t^n(t)\|^{\rho}u_t^n(t)\right\|=\|u_t^n(t)\|^{\rho+1}\leq C\left(\|(u_0;u_1)\|_{\mathcal{H}_1}\right),
\]
since \(\|u_t^n(t)\|\leq C\) by \eqref{bc8} and the function \(s\mapsto s^{\rho+1}\) is continuous on \([0,\infty)\) with \(\rho+1>0\). Moreover,
\begin{align*}
 \left\|\int_{0}^{t}g(t-s)A^{\frac12}u^n(s)ds\right\|_1
&=\left\|A^{\frac12}\int_{0}^{t}g(t-s)A^{\frac12}u^n(s)ds\right\|
\leq\int_{0}^{t}g(t-s)\|Au^n(s)\|ds
\\
&\leq G_0\|Au^n\|_{L^\infty(0,\infty;V_0)}
\leq C\left(\|(u_0;u_1)\|_{\mathcal{H}_1}\right).
\end{align*}
Therefore, there exist a subsequence of \(\{u^n\}\), still denoted by \(\{u^n\}\), a function \(u\in L^{\infty}(0,\infty;V_2)\) with \(u_t\in L^{\infty}(0,\infty;V_1)\), and a function \(\chi\in L^\infty(0,\infty;V_0)\) such that, as \(n\to\infty\),
\begin{equation}\label{strongsolu}
\left\{
\begin{split}
&u^n\rightharpoonup u\quad \text{weakly star in }L^{\infty}(0,\infty;V_2),\\
&u_t^n\rightharpoonup u_t\quad \text{weakly star in }L^{\infty}(0,\infty;V_1),\\
&u_{tt}^n\rightharpoonup u_{tt}\quad \text{weakly star in }L^{\infty}(0,\infty;V_{0}),\\
&\int_{0}^{t}g(t-s)A^{\frac12}u^n(s)ds\rightharpoonup\int_{0}^{t}g(t-s)A^{\frac12}u(s)ds\quad \\
&\qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad\text{weakly star in }L^{\infty}(0,\infty;V_1),\\
&\|u_t^n\|^{\rho}u_t^n\rightharpoonup\chi\quad \text{weakly star in }L^{\infty}(0,\infty;V_0).
\end{split}
\right.
\end{equation}

Since \(V_2\hookrightarrow V_1\hookrightarrow V_0\) compactly, the Aubin--Lions--Simon theorem \cite{MR0916688} together with \eqref{bc8} and \eqref{strongsolu} yields, after passing to a subsequence,
\begin{equation}\label{bc5}
\begin{split}
&u_{t}^n\rightarrow u_{t}\quad \text{strongly in }C([0,T];V_{0})\text{ for every }T>0,\\
&u^n\rightarrow u\quad \text{strongly in }C([0,T];V_{1})\text{ for every }T>0.
\end{split}
\end{equation}
In particular, \(u^n(0)\to u(0)\) strongly in \(V_1\) and \(u^n_t(0)\to u_t(0)\) strongly in \(V_{0}\). By \eqref{defineun},
\begin{equation}\label{initialdy}
u(0)=u_0,\qquad u_t(0)=u_1.
\end{equation}

We next identify the weak limit \(\chi\). Since \(l:V_0\to V_0\) is monotone and semicontinuous, we argue as in the classical monotone operator method. For any \(\varphi\in L^2(0,t;V_0)\), the monotonicity of \(l\) gives
\[
\int_{0}^{t}\left(\|u_{\tau}^n\|^{\rho}u_{\tau}^n-\|\varphi\|^{\rho}\varphi,u_{\tau}^n-\varphi\right)d\tau\geq0.
\]
Taking \(\liminf\) as \(n\to\infty\), and using \eqref{strongsolu} and \eqref{bc5}, we obtain
\[
\int_{0}^{t}\left(\chi-\|\varphi\|^{\rho}\varphi,u_{\tau}-\varphi\right)d\tau\geq0.
\]
Here we used that \(\|u_{\tau}^n\|^{\rho}u_{\tau}^n\rightharpoonup\chi\) weakly in \(L^2(0,t;V_0)\) and \(u_{\tau}^n\to u_{\tau}\) strongly in \(L^2(0,t;V_0)\), so that the product converges. Choosing \(\varphi=u_\tau-\lambda\omega\) with \(\lambda\geq0\) and \(\omega\in L^2(0,t;V_0)\), and then letting \(\lambda\to0^+\), we get
\[
\int_{0}^{t}\left(\chi-\|u_\tau\|^{\rho}u_\tau,\omega\right)d\tau\geq0.
\]
Repeating the argument with \(\lambda\leq0\) yields the reverse inequality. Hence
\begin{equation}\label{chiey}
\chi=\|u_t\|^{\rho}u_t.
\end{equation}

Now, letting \(n\to\infty\) in \eqref{weak}, and using \eqref{strongsolu} and \eqref{chiey}, we obtain
\[
(u_{tt}(t),\omega_k)+(Au(t),\omega_k)-\left(\int_{0}^{t}g(t-s)Au(s)ds,\omega_k\right)+\|u_t\|^{\rho}(u_t,\omega_k)=0
\]
for \(t\in(0,\infty)\) and \(k=1,2,\cdots\). Since \(\{\omega_k\}_{k=1}^\infty\) is a basis of \(V_0\), it follows that
\[
u_{tt}(t)+Au(t)-\int_{0}^{t}g(t-s)Au(s)ds+\|u_t\|^{\rho}u_t=0
\]
holds in \(V_0\) for almost every \(t\in(0,\infty)\). Together with \eqref{initialdy}, this proves the existence part of the theorem.

Moreover, the above estimates show that \((u;u_t)\in L^{\infty}(0,\infty;\mathcal{H}_1)\) and \(u_{tt}\in L^{\infty}(0,\infty;V_0)\). Since \(u\in L^\infty(0,\infty;V_2)\), \(u_t\in L^\infty(0,\infty;V_1)\), we have \(u\in W^{1,\infty}(0,T;V_1)\subset C([0,T];V_1)\) for every \(T>0\). Similarly, since \(u_t\in L^\infty(0,\infty;V_1)\) and \(u_{tt}\in L^\infty(0,\infty;V_0)\), we have \(u_t\in W^{1,\infty}(0,T;V_0)\subset C([0,T];V_0)\) for every \(T>0\). Thus \(u\in C([0,\infty);V_1)\) and \(u_t\in C([0,\infty);V_0)\), which matches Definition~\ref{defweak}.

It remains to prove uniqueness. Let \(u\) and \(v\) be two global solutions of \eqref{abstract} with initial data \(z_0=(u_0;u_1)\in\mathcal{H}_1\) and \(\widetilde{z}_0=(v_0;v_1)\in\mathcal{H}_1\), respectively, and set \(\omega:=u-v\). Then
\begin{equation}\label{unique}
\omega_{tt}+A\omega-\int_{0}^{t}g(t-s)A\omega(s)ds+\|u_t\|^{\rho}u_t-\|v_t\|^{\rho}v_t=0.
\end{equation}
Taking the multiplier \(\omega_t\) in \eqref{unique}, we obtain
\[
\frac12\frac{d}{dt}\left(\|\omega_t\|^2+\|A^{1/2}\omega\|^2\right)
-\left(\int_0^t g(t-s)A\omega(s)ds,\omega_t\right)
+\left(\|u_t\|^\rho u_t-\|v_t\|^\rho v_t,\omega_t\right)=0.
\]
Define
\begin{align*}
 E_\omega(t):=&\frac12\left(\|\omega_t(t)\|^2+\left(1-\int_0^t g(s)ds\right)\|A^{1/2}\omega(t)\|^2\right)\\
&+\frac12\int_0^t g(t-s)\|A^{1/2}\omega(t)-A^{1/2}\omega(s)\|^2ds.
\end{align*}
Using the standard identity for the memory term, we get
\begin{align*}
E_\omega'(t)&+\left(\|u_t\|^\rho u_t-\|v_t\|^\rho v_t,\omega_t\right)\\
&+\frac12g(t)\|A^{1/2}\omega(t)\|^2
-\frac12\int_0^t g'(t-s)\|A^{1/2}\omega(t)-A^{1/2}\omega(s)\|^2ds=0.
\end{align*}
Equivalently,
\begin{align*}
 E_\omega'(t)
=
&-\left(\|u_t\|^\rho u_t-\|v_t\|^\rho v_t,\omega_t\right)\\
&-\frac12g(t)\|A^{1/2}\omega(t)\|^2
+\frac12\int_0^t g'(t-s)\|A^{1/2}\omega(t)-A^{1/2}\omega(s)\|^2ds.
\end{align*}
By Lemma \ref{continuity}, the map \(l(v)=\|v\|^\rho v\) is monotone for \(\rho>-1\). Hence
\[
\left(\|u_t\|^\rho u_t-\|v_t\|^\rho v_t,\omega_t\right)
=(l(u_t)-l(v_t),u_t-v_t)\ge0.
\]
Since \(g\ge0\) and \(g'\le0\), we deduce that \(E_\omega'(t)\le0\). But \(E_\omega(0)=0\) and \(E_\omega(t)\ge0\), so \(E_\omega(t)=0\) for all \(t\ge0\). Therefore \(\omega\equiv0\), and uniqueness follows for every \(\rho>-1\).

body_md:
Using \eqref{abstract} and the definition of \(I_1\), together with Young's inequality and \eqref{embed} with \(s_1=1\) and \(s_2=0\), we obtain
\begin{align}
\frac{d}{dt}I_1(t)
&=-\int_{0}^{t}g(s)ds\|u_t(t)\|^2
-\left(u_{tt},\int_{0}^{t}g(t-s)(u(t)-u(s))ds\right)\notag\\
&\quad-\left(u_t(t),\int_{0}^{t}g'(t-s)(u(t)-u(s))ds\right)\notag\\
&=-\int_{0}^{t}g(s)ds\|u_t(t)\|^2
+\left(A u(t),\int_{0}^{t}g(t-s)(u(t)-u(s))ds\right)\notag\\
&\quad-\left(\int_{0}^{t}g(t-s)A u(s)ds,\int_{0}^{t}g(t-s)(u(t)-u(s))ds\right)\notag\\
&\quad+\|u_t(t)\|^{\rho}\left(u_t(t),\int_{0}^{t}g(t-s)(u(t)-u(s))ds\right)\notag\\
&\quad-\left(u_t(t),\int_{0}^{t}g'(t-s)(u(t)-u(s))ds\right)\notag\\
&=-\int_{0}^{t}g(s)ds\|u_t(t)\|^2\notag\\
&\quad+\left(A^{\frac12}u(t),\int_{0}^{t}g(t-s)(A^{\frac12}u(t)-A^{\frac12}u(s))ds\right)\notag\\
&\quad-\left(\int_{0}^{t}g(t-s)A^{\frac12}u(s)ds,\int_{0}^{t}g(t-s)(A^{\frac12}u(t)-A^{\frac12}u(s))ds\right)\notag\\
&\quad+\|u_t(t)\|^{\rho}\left(u_t(t),\int_{0}^{t}g(t-s)(u(t)-u(s))ds\right)\notag\\
&\quad-\left(u_t(t),\int_{0}^{t}g'(t-s)(u(t)-u(s))ds\right).\notag
\end{align}

Using the decomposition
\[
A^{\frac12}u(t)
=\left(1-\int_{0}^{t}g(s)ds\right)A^{\frac12}u(t)
+\int_{0}^{t}g(t-s)A^{\frac12}u(t)ds,
\]
we combine the second and third terms on the right-hand side as
\begin{align}
&\left(A^{\frac12}u(t),\int_{0}^{t}g(t-s)(A^{\frac12}u(t)-A^{\frac12}u(s))ds\right)\notag\\
&\quad-\left(\int_{0}^{t}g(t-s)A^{\frac12}u(s)ds,\int_{0}^{t}g(t-s)(A^{\frac12}u(t)-A^{\frac12}u(s))ds\right)\notag\\
&=\left(\left(1-\int_{0}^{t}g(s)ds\right)A^{\frac12}u(t),
\int_{0}^{t}g(t-s)(A^{\frac12}u(t)-A^{\frac12}u(s))ds\right)\notag\\
&\quad+\left\|\int_{0}^{t}g(t-s)(A^{\frac12}u(t)-A^{\frac12}u(s))ds\right\|^2.\notag
\end{align}
Hence
\begin{align}
\frac{d}{dt}I_1(t)
&=-\int_{0}^{t}g(s)ds\|u_t(t)\|^2\notag\\
&\quad+\left(\left(1-\int_{0}^{t}g(s)ds\right)A^{\frac12}u(t),
\int_{0}^{t}g(t-s)(A^{\frac12}u(t)-A^{\frac12}u(s))ds\right)\notag\\
&\quad+\left\|\int_{0}^{t}g(t-s)(A^{\frac12}u(t)-A^{\frac12}u(s))ds\right\|^2\notag\\
&\quad+\|u_t(t)\|^{\rho}\left(u_t(t),\int_{0}^{t}g(t-s)(u(t)-u(s))ds\right)\notag\\
&\quad-\left(u_t(t),\int_{0}^{t}g'(t-s)(u(t)-u(s))ds\right)\notag\\
&\leq-\int_{0}^{t}g(s)ds\|u_t(t)\|^2\notag\\
&\quad+\varepsilon_1\|A^{\frac12}u(t)\|^2
+\widetilde C(\varepsilon_1)\left\|\int_{0}^{t}g(t-s)(A^{\frac12}u(t)-A^{\frac12}u(s))ds\right\|^2\notag\\
&\quad+\left\|\int_{0}^{t}g(t-s)(A^{\frac12}u(t)-A^{\frac12}u(s))ds\right\|^2\notag\\
&\quad+\frac12\|u_t(t)\|^{2\rho+2}
+\frac12\left\|\int_{0}^{t}g(t-s)(u(t)-u(s))ds\right\|^2\notag\\
&\quad+\frac{G_0}{4}\|u_t(t)\|^2
+\frac{1}{G_0}\left\|\int_{0}^{t}-g'(t-s)(u(t)-u(s))ds\right\|^2.\notag
\end{align}
By the embedding \(\|u(t)-u(s)\|\le \lambda_1^{-1/2}\|A^{1/2}u(t)-A^{1/2}u(s)\|\), we have
\begin{align}
&\frac12\left\|\int_{0}^{t}g(t-s)(u(t)-u(s))ds\right\|^2
\leq \frac{1}{2\lambda_1}\left\|\int_{0}^{t}g(t-s)(A^{\frac12}u(t)-A^{\frac12}u(s))ds\right\|^2,\notag\\
&\frac{1}{G_0}\left\|\int_{0}^{t}-g'(t-s)(u(t)-u(s))ds\right\|^2
\leq \frac{1}{\lambda_1G_0}\left\|\int_{0}^{t}-g'(t-s)(A^{\frac12}u(t)-A^{\frac12}u(s))ds\right\|^2.\notag
\end{align}
Combining the above estimates, we arrive at
\begin{align}
\frac{d}{dt}I_1(t)
&\leq\left(-\int_{0}^{t}g(s)ds+\frac{G_0}{4}\right)\|u_t(t)\|^2
+\varepsilon_1\|A^{\frac12}u(t)\|^2
+\frac12\|u_t(t)\|^{2\rho+2}\notag\\
&\quad+\hat C(\varepsilon_1)\left\|\int_{0}^{t}g(t-s)(A^{\frac12}u(t)-A^{\frac12}u(s))ds\right\|^2\notag\\
&\quad+\frac{1}{\lambda_1G_0}\left\|\int_{0}^{t}-g'(t-s)(A^{\frac12}u(t)-A^{\frac12}u(s))ds\right\|^2,\notag
\end{align}
where
\[
\hat C(\varepsilon_1)=\widetilde C(\varepsilon_1)+1+\frac{1}{2\lambda_1}.
\]
Here we used Young's inequality in the form
\[
\|u_t\|^{\rho+1}\left\|\int_0^t g(t-s)(u(t)-u(s))ds\right\|
\le \frac12\|u_t\|^{2\rho+2}
+\frac12\left\|\int_0^t g(t-s)(u(t)-u(s))ds\right\|^2,
\]
together with the embedding \(\|u(t)-u(s)\|\le \lambda_1^{-1/2}\|A^{1/2}u(t)-A^{1/2}u(s)\|\).

Since \(t\geq t_0\), \eqref{existencet0} gives
\[
-\int_{0}^{t}g(s)ds+\frac{G_0}{4}
\leq-\int_{0}^{t_0}g(s)ds+\frac{G_0}{4}
=-\frac{G_0}{4}.
\]
Hence the coefficient of \(\|u_t(t)\|^2\) is bounded by \(-\frac{G_0}{4}\).

Next, by the definition of \(K_\delta\) and \(M(\delta)\), together with H\"older's inequality,
\begin{align}
&\left\|\int_{0}^{t}g(t-s)\left(A^{\frac12}u(t)-A^{\frac12}u(s)\right)ds\right\|^2\nonumber\\
=&\left\|\int_{0}^{t}\frac{g(t-s)}{\sqrt{K_\delta(t-s)}}\sqrt{K_\delta(t-s)}\left(A^{\frac12}u(t)-A^{\frac12}u(s)\right)ds\right\|^2\nonumber\\
\leq&\int_{0}^{t}\frac{g^2(t-s)}{K_\delta(t-s)}ds\int_0^tK_\delta(t-s)\left\|A^{\frac12}u(t)-A^{\frac12}u(s)\right\|^2ds\nonumber\\
=&M(\delta)\int_0^tK_\delta(t-s)\left\|A^{\frac12}u(t)-A^{\frac12}u(s)\right\|^2ds.\label{Kd}
\end{align}
Also, since \(-g'\ge0\) and \(\int_0^t -g'(t-s)ds\le g(0)\),
\begin{align*}
&\left\|\int_{0}^{t}-g'(t-s)\left(A^{\frac12}u(t)-A^{\frac12}u(s)\right)ds\right\|^2\\
=&\left\|\int_{0}^{t}\sqrt{-g'(t-s)}\sqrt{-g'(t-s)}\left(A^{\frac12}u(t)-A^{\frac12}u(s)\right)ds\right\|^2\\
&\leq\int_0^t-g'(t-s)ds\int_0^t-g'(t-s)\left\|A^{\frac12}u(t)-A^{\frac12}u(s)\right\|^2ds\\
&\leq g(0)\int_{0}^{t}-g'(t-s)\left\|A^{\frac12}u(t)-A^{\frac12}u(s)\right\|^2ds.
\end{align*}
Inserting these two estimates into the previous inequality and absorbing the constant \(\frac12\) into \(C\), we obtain
\begin{align*}
\frac{d}{dt}I_1(t)
&\leq-\frac{G_0}{4}\|u_t(t)\|^2+\varepsilon_1\left\|A^{\frac12}u(t)\right\|^2+C\|u_t(t)\|^{2\rho+2}\\
&\quad+\hat C(\varepsilon_1)M(\delta)\int_{0}^{t}K_\delta(t-s)\left\|A^{\frac12}u(t)-A^{\frac12}u(s)\right\|^2ds\\
&\quad-\frac{g(0)}{\lambda_1G_0}\int_{0}^{t}g'(t-s)\left\|A^{\frac12}u(t)-A^{\frac12}u(s)\right\|^2ds,
\end{align*}
where we used \(g'\le0\), so that \(-g'\ge0\) and the last term is nonnegative. This yields \eqref{I1esti}. The proof is complete.

body_md:
From \eqref{abstract}, Young's inequality, and \eqref{embed} with \(s_1=1\) and \(s_2=0\), we deduce that, for any \(\epsilon>0\),
\begin{align*}
\frac{d}{dt}I_2(t)
&=\left(u_{tt}(t),u(t)\right)+\|u_t(t)\|^2\\
&=-\left(u(t),Au(t)\right)\\
&\quad+\left(\int_{0}^{t}g(t-s)Au(s)ds,u(t)\right)-\left(\|u_t(t)\|^{\rho}u_t(t),u(t)\right)+\|u_t(t)\|^2\\
&=-\left\|A^{\frac12}u(t)\right\|^2\\
&\quad+\left(\int_{0}^{t}g(t-s)A^{\frac12}u(s)ds,A^{\frac12}u(t)\right)-\left(\|u_t(t)\|^{\rho}u_t(t),u(t)\right)+\|u_t(t)\|^2\\
&=-\left\|A^{\frac12}u(t)\right\|^2-\left(\|u_t(t)\|^{\rho}u_t(t),u(t)\right)+\|u_t(t)\|^2\\
&\quad+\left(\int_{0}^{t}g(t-s)(A^{\frac12}u(s)-A^{\frac12}u(t))ds,A^{\frac12}u(t)\right)+\int_{0}^{t}g(s)ds\|A^{\frac12}u(t)\|^2.
\end{align*}
For the nonlocal damping term, by \(\|u(t)\|\le\lambda_1^{-1/2}\|A^{1/2}u(t)\|\) and Young's inequality,
\[
\left|\left(\|u_t(t)\|^{\rho}u_t(t),u(t)\right)\right|
\le \epsilon\|A^{\frac12}u(t)\|^2+C(\epsilon)\|u_t(t)\|^{2\rho+2},
\]
where \(C(\epsilon)\) depends only on \(\epsilon,\lambda_1\). For the memory term, by Young's inequality,
\begin{align*}
&\left|\left(\int_{0}^{t}g(t-s)(A^{\frac12}u(s)-A^{\frac12}u(t))ds,A^{\frac12}u(t)\right)\right|\\
&\qquad \le \epsilon\|A^{\frac12}u(t)\|^2+C(\epsilon)\left\|\int_{0}^{t}g(t-s)(A^{\frac12}u(t)-A^{\frac12}u(s))ds\right\|^2.
\end{align*}
Combining these estimates, we obtain
\begin{align*}
\frac{d}{dt}I_2(t)
&\leq-\left(1-\int_0^t g(s)ds-2\epsilon\right)\left\|A^{\frac12}u(t)\right\|^2+\|u_t(t)\|^2\\
&\quad+C(\epsilon)\|u_t(t)\|^{2\rho+2}
+C(\epsilon)\left\|\int_{0}^{t}g(t-s)(A^{\frac12}u(t)-A^{\frac12}u(s))ds\right\|^2.
\end{align*}
By \eqref{mu_0}, we may choose \(\epsilon=\frac{\mu_0}{8}\) so that
\[
1-\int_0^t g(s)ds-2\epsilon\geq\mu_0-2\epsilon\geq\frac{3\mu_0}{4}\geq\frac{\mu_0}{2}.
\]
Combining this with \eqref{Kd}, which gives
\[
\left\|\int_0^t g(t-s)(A^{1/2}u(t)-A^{1/2}u(s))ds\right\|^2
\le M(\delta)\int_0^t K_\delta(t-s)\left\|A^{1/2}u(t)-A^{1/2}u(s)\right\|^2ds,
\]
we obtain \eqref{I2}, with a constant \(C\) depending only on \(\mu_0,\lambda_1\).

\begin{align*}
&-2\left(A^{\frac12}u(t),\int_{0}^{t}\sqrt{g(t-s)}\sqrt{g(t-s)}\left(A^{\frac12}u(s)-A^{\frac12}u(t)\right)ds\right)\\

body_md:
Define
\[
J(t):=N_1I_1(t)+N_2I_2(t)+I_3(t)+N_4I_4(t),
\]
where \(I_i\), \(i=1,2,3,4\), are the functionals defined above, and \(N_1,N_2,N_4\) are positive constants to be determined.

Using \eqref{ed}, \eqref{I1esti}, \eqref{I2}, \eqref{I3}, and \eqref{I4}, we obtain, for \(t\geq t_0\),
\begin{align*}
\frac{d}{dt}J(t)
&\leq\left(N_1\varepsilon_1-\frac{N_2\mu_0}{2}+3G_0+3N_4G_0\delta M(\delta)\right)\left\|A^{\frac12}u(t)\right\|^2
+\left(-\frac{N_1G_0}{4}+N_2\right)\|u_t(t)\|^2\\
&\quad+\left(N_1\hat C(\varepsilon_1)M(\delta)+N_2CM(\delta)-\frac{N_4M(\delta)}{2}\right)\int_{0}^{t}K_{\delta}(t-s)\left\|A^{\frac12}u(t)-A^{\frac12}u(s)\right\|^2ds\\
&\quad-\frac12\int_{0}^{t}g(t-s)\left\|A^{\frac12}u(t)-A^{\frac12}u(s)\right\|^2ds+(N_1+N_2)C\|u_t(t)\|^{2\rho+2}\\
&\quad-N_1\frac{g(0)}{\lambda_1G_0}\int_{0}^{t}g'(t-s)\left\|A^{\frac12}u(t)-A^{\frac12}u(s)\right\|^2ds.
\end{align*}
Here the coefficient of \(\|A^{1/2}u\|^2\) is obtained by summing the contributions
\[
N_1\varepsilon_1,\qquad -\frac{N_2\mu_0}{2},\qquad 3G_0,\qquad 3N_4G_0\delta M(\delta),
\]
from \(I_1,I_2,I_3,I_4\), respectively.

By (AG), for almost every \(s\in(0,\infty)\),
\[
\frac{\delta g^2(s)}{-g'(s)+\delta g(s)}\leq g(s)\in L^1(0,\infty).
\]
Hence, by \eqref{K}, \eqref{M}, and the dominated convergence theorem,
\[
\lim_{\delta\to 0}\delta M(\delta)=\lim_{\delta\to 0}\int_0^{\infty}\frac{\delta g^2(s)}{-g'(s)+\delta g(s)}ds=0.
\]
We may therefore choose \(\delta\) small enough such that
\begin{equation}\label{deltamdelta}
3N_4G_0\delta M(\delta)\leq\frac{N_2\mu_0}{8}.
\end{equation}
Moreover, choosing
\[
\varepsilon_1=\frac{N_2\mu_0}{8N_1},\qquad
N_2=\frac{48G_0}{\mu_0},\qquad
N_1=\frac{4N_2+1}{G_0},\qquad
N_4=2(N_1\hat C(\varepsilon_1)+N_2C)+1,
\]
we obtain
\[
N_1\varepsilon_1=\frac{N_2\mu_0}{8}=6G_0,\qquad
3N_4G_0\delta M(\delta)\leq\frac{N_2\mu_0}{8}=6G_0.
\]
Hence
\[
\frac{N_2\mu_0}{2}-N_1\varepsilon_1-3G_0-3N_4G_0\delta M(\delta)
\geq24G_0-6G_0-3G_0-6G_0=9G_0>0.
\]
Therefore, for \(t\geq t_0\),
\begin{align*}
\frac{d}{dt}J(t)
&\leq-9G_0\|A^{\frac12}u(t)\|^2-\frac14\|u_t(t)\|^2\\
&\quad-\frac12\int_{0}^{t}g(t-s)\left\|A^{\frac12}u(t)-A^{\frac12}u(s)\right\|^2ds+(N_1+N_2)C\|u_t(t)\|^{2\rho+2}\\
&\quad-N_1\frac{g(0)}{\lambda_1G_0}\int_{0}^{t}g'(t-s)\left\|A^{\frac12}u(t)-A^{\frac12}u(s)\right\|^2ds.
\end{align*}
Since
\[
E(t)\geq\frac12\|u_t\|^2+\frac{\mu_0}{2}\|A^{\frac12}u\|^2+\frac12\int_{0}^{t}g(t-s)\left\|A^{\frac12}u(t)-A^{\frac12}u(s)\right\|^2ds,
\]
\[
-E'(t)\geq\|u_t(t)\|^{\rho+2},\qquad
-E'(t)\geq-\frac12\int_{0}^{t}g'(t-s)\left\|A^{\frac12}u(t)-A^{\frac12}u(s)\right\|^2ds,
\]
and, since \(-1<\rho<0\), we have \(\rho+2\in(1,2)\), so that
\[
\|u_t(t)\|^{2\rho+2}\le C(-E'(t))^{\frac{2\rho+2}{\rho+2}}.
\]
Indeed, by \eqref{ed} and \(g'\le0\),
\[
-E'(t)\ge\|u_t(t)\|^{\rho+2},
\]
and raising both sides to the power \(\frac{2\rho+2}{\rho+2}>0\) gives the claim. Hence we deduce, for \(t\geq t_0\),
\begin{align}
\frac{d}{dt}J(t)
&\leq-CE(t)-C\int_{0}^{t}g(t-s)\left\|A^{\frac12}u(s)\right\|^2ds-CE'(t)+C(-E'(t))^{\frac{2\rho+2}{\rho+2}}.\label{J}
\end{align}
Here the constant \(C>0\) depends only on \(\rho,\mu_0,\lambda_1,G_0,g(0),N_1,N_2,N_4,\hat C(\varepsilon_1)\).

Set
\[
L(t):=NE(t)+J(t)=NE(t)+N_1I_1(t)+N_2I_2(t)+I_3(t)+N_4I_4(t),
\]
where \(N\) is a positive constant to be determined. By the definitions of \(E\) and \(I_1\), Young's inequality, H\"older's inequality, and \eqref{embed} with \(s_1=1\) and \(s_2=0\), we have
\begin{align*}
|I_1(t)|
&=\left|\left(u_t(t),\int_{0}^{t}g(t-s)(u(t)-u(s))ds\right)\right|\\
&\leq C\|u_t(t)\|^2+C\left\|\int_{0}^{t}\sqrt{g(t-s)}\sqrt{g(t-s)}\left(u(t)-u(s)\right)ds\right\|^2\\
&\leq C\|u_t(t)\|^2+C\underbrace{\int_0^{\infty}g(s)ds}_{=G_0}\int_{0}^{t}g(t-s)\left\|A^{\frac12}u(t)-A^{\frac12}u(s)\right\|^2ds\\
&\leq CE(t),
\end{align*}
where \(C\) depends only on \(G_0,\lambda_1\). Similarly, \(|I_2(t)|\leq CE(t)\), with \(C\) depending only on \(\lambda_1\). Moreover, \(I_3(t),I_4(t)\geq0\). Hence, choosing \(N\) sufficiently large, we obtain
\begin{equation}\label{Lda}
L(t)\geq CE(t),
\end{equation}
where the constant \(C>0\) depends on \(N_1,N_2,G_0,\lambda_1\).

By (AG), \(\lim_{t\to\infty}g(t)=0\), and \(g'(t)\leq-kg(t)\) for almost every \(t\in[0,\infty)\). Thus, by \eqref{G},
\[
G(t)=\int_t^{\infty}g(s)ds\leq-\frac{1}{k}\int_t^{\infty}g'(s)ds=\frac1k g(t).
\]
Using the definitions of \(I_3\) and \(I_4\), together with \eqref{deltamdelta}, we get
\[
I_3(t)\leq C\int_{0}^{t}g(t-s)\left\|A^{\frac12}u(s)\right\|^2ds,\qquad
I_4(t)\leq CE(t)+C\int_{0}^{t}g(t-s)\left\|A^{\frac12}u(s)\right\|^2ds.
\]
Since
\begin{align*}
\int_{0}^{t}g(t-s)\left\|A^{\frac12}u(s)\right\|^2ds
&=\int_{0}^{t}g(t-s)\left\|A^{\frac12}u(s)-A^{\frac12}u(t)+A^{\frac12}u(t)\right\|^2ds\\
&\leq2\int_{0}^{t}g(t-s)\left\|A^{\frac12}u(s)-A^{\frac12}u(t)\right\|^2ds\\
&\quad+2\int_{0}^{t}g(t-s)ds\left\|A^{\frac12}u(t)\right\|^2\\
&\leq CE(t),
\end{align*}
we obtain
\begin{align}
C_1E(t)\leq L(t)\leq C_2E(t)\label{dj}
\end{align}
for some constants \(C_1,C_2>0\) depending only on \(\rho,\mu_0,\lambda_1,G_0,g(0),k\) and on \(M(\delta)\).

From \eqref{J} and \eqref{dj}, for \(t\geq t_0\), and choosing \(N\) sufficiently large so that \(N-C\geq0\), we get
\begin{align}
\frac{d}{dt}L(t)
&=NE'(t)+J'(t)\notag\\
&\leq-CE(t)-C\int_{0}^{t}g(t-s)\left\|A^{\frac12}u(s)\right\|^2ds\notag\\
&\quad+(N-C)E'(t)+C(-E'(t))^{\frac{2\rho+2}{\rho+2}}\notag\\
&\leq-CL(t)+C(-E'(t))^{\frac{2\rho+2}{\rho+2}}.\label{betterrs}
\end{align}
Since \(-1<\rho<0\), multiplying \eqref{betterrs} by \(L^{\frac{-\rho}{2\rho+2}}(t)\) and integrating over \([t,T]\) with \(T>t\geq t_0\), we obtain, by Young's inequality,
\begin{align*}
\frac{2\rho+2}{\rho+2}\left(L^{\frac{\rho+2}{2\rho+2}}(T)-L^{\frac{\rho+2}{2\rho+2}}(t)\right)
&\leq-C\int_{t}^{T}L^{\frac{\rho+2}{2\rho+2}}(s)ds+C\int_{t}^{T}L^{\frac{-\rho}{2\rho+2}}(s)(-E'(s))^{\frac{2\rho+2}{\rho+2}}ds\\
&\leq-C\int_{t}^{T}L^{\frac{\rho+2}{2\rho+2}}(s)ds\\
&\quad+\frac{C}{2}\int_{t}^{T}L^{\frac{\rho+2}{2\rho+2}}(s)ds+\mathcal{C}(\rho)\int_{t}^{T}(-E'(s))ds,
\end{align*}
which, together with \eqref{dj}, implies
\begin{align*}
\int_{t}^{T}L^{\frac{\rho+2}{2\rho+2}}(s)ds
&\leq CL^{\frac{\rho+2}{2\rho+2}}(t)+C\int_{t}^{T}(-E'(s))ds\\
&\leq CL^{\frac{\rho+2}{2\rho+2}}(t)+CE(t)
\leq C\left(L^{\frac{\rho+2}{2\rho+2}-1}(t)+1\right)L(t)
\\
&=C\left(L^{\frac{-\rho}{2\rho+2}}(t)+1\right)L(t).
\end{align*}
Hence, since \(L(t)\leq C_2E(t)\leq C_2E(0)\),
\[
\int_{t}^{T}L^{\frac{\rho+2}{2\rho+2}}(s)ds\leq C\left(1+E(0)^{\frac{-\rho}{2\rho+2}}\right)L(t).
\]
By \eqref{dj},
\begin{align}
\int_{t}^{T}E^{\frac{\rho+2}{2\rho+2}}(s)ds\leq C\left(1+E(0)^{\frac{-\rho}{2\rho+2}}\right)E(t)\leq C\left(1+E(0)^{\frac{-\rho}{2\rho+2}}\right)E(0).\label{case1plo}
\end{align}
Taking \(T=2t\), and using \(E'(t)\leq0\), we get
\[
[E(2t)]^{\frac{\rho+2}{2\rho+2}}t\leq C\left(1+E(0)^{\frac{-\rho}{2\rho+2}}\right)E(0),
\]
so that
\[
E(2t)\leq(2C)^{\frac{2\rho+2}{\rho+2}}\left(1+E(0)^{\frac{-\rho}{2\rho+2}}\right)^{\frac{2\rho+2}{\rho+2}}E(0)^{\frac{2\rho+2}{\rho+2}}(2t)^{-\frac{2\rho+2}{\rho+2}}.
\]
Repeating the above iteration \(m\) times yields
\begin{align}
E(t)\leq t^{-\sum\limits_{i=1}^{m}\left(\frac{2\rho+2}{\rho+2}\right)^i}E^{\left(\frac{2\rho+2}{\rho+2}\right)^m}(0)C^{\sum\limits_{i=1}^{m}\left(\frac{2\rho+2}{\rho+2}\right)^i}\left(1+E(0)^{\frac{-\rho}{2\rho+2}}\right)^{\sum\limits_{i=1}^{m}\left(\frac{2\rho+2}{\rho+2}\right)^i}2^{\sum\limits_{i=1}^{m}i\left(\frac{2\rho+2}{\rho+2}\right)^i}.\label{case1plo01}
\end{align}
Let
\[
q:=\frac{2\rho+2}{\rho+2}.
\]
Since \(-1<\rho<0\), we have \(0<q<1\). Therefore, as \(m\to\infty\),
\[
\sum\limits_{i=1}^{m}q^i\to\frac{q}{1-q}=-\frac{2\rho+2}{\rho},\qquad
q^m\to0,\qquad
\sum\limits_{i=1}^{m}iq^i\to\frac{q}{(1-q)^2}=\frac{(2\rho+2)(\rho+2)}{\rho^2}.
\]
Letting \(m\to\infty\) in \eqref{case1plo01}, we conclude
\[
E(t)\leq t^{\frac{2\rho+2}{\rho}}C^{-\frac{2\rho+2}{\rho}}\left(1+E(0)^{\frac{-\rho}{2\rho+2}}\right)^{-\frac{2\rho+2}{\rho}}2^{\frac{(2\rho+2)(\rho+2)}{\rho^2}}.
\]
Thus there exists a constant
\[
C(\rho,\mu_0,\lambda_1,g(0),G_0,k)>0
\]
such that
\[
E(t)\leq C(\rho,\mu_0,\lambda_1,g(0),G_0,k)
\left(1+E(0)^{\frac{-\rho}{2\rho+2}}\right)^{-\frac{2\rho+2}{\rho}}
t^{\frac{2\rho+2}{\rho}},\qquad t\ge t_0.
\]
Since \(-\frac{2\rho+2}{\rho}=\frac{2\rho+2}{|\rho|}>0\) and
\(-\frac{\rho}{2\rho+2}\in(0,\frac12)\), we have
\[
E(0)^{\frac{-\rho}{2\rho+2}}\le 1+E(0)^{-1},
\]
and hence
\[
\left(1+E(0)^{-\frac{\rho}{2\rho+2}}\right)^{\frac{2\rho+2}{|\rho|}}
\le C(\rho)\left(1+E(0)^{-1}\right)^{\frac{2\rho+2}{|\rho|}}.
\]
Consequently,
\[
E(t)\leq C(\rho,\mu_0,\lambda_1,g(0),G_0,k)
\left(1+E(0)^{-1}\right)^{\frac{2\rho+2}{|\rho|}}
t^{\frac{2\rho+2}{\rho}},\qquad t\ge t_0.
\]
This completes the proof for \(-1<\rho<0\).

title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lemmp}
Let \(\phi:[0,\infty)\to\mathbb{R}\) be a nonnegative and bounded function satisfying
\[
\sup_{t\leq s\leq t+1}[\phi(s)]^{1+\sigma}\leq c_0[\phi(t)-\phi(t+1)],\qquad t\geq0,
\]
where \(c_0>0\) and \(\sigma\geq0\) are constants. Then:
\begin{description}
\item[(i)] if \(\sigma>0\),
\[
\phi(t)\leq\left[\left(\sup_{0\leq s\leq1}\phi(s)\right)^{-\sigma}+\frac{\sigma}{c_0}(t-1)^+\right]^{-1/\sigma},\qquad t\geq0;
\]
\item[(ii)] if \(\sigma=0\),
\[
\phi(t)\leq\left(\sup_{0\leq s\leq1}\phi(s)\right)e^{-\kappa(t-1)^+},\qquad t\geq0,
\]
where \(\kappa=-\log(1-1/c_0)\). Here \(s^+:=\frac12(s+|s|)\).
\end{description}

title: Proof
body_md:
From (AG) and \eqref{ed}, we infer that
\begin{align}
\int_{t}^{t+1}\|u_t(s)\|^{\rho+2}ds
&\leq\int_{t}^{t+1}\left(\frac12g(s)\left\|A^{\frac12}u(s)\right\|^2+\|u_t(s)\|^{\rho+2}\right.\notag\\
&\quad\left.-\frac12\int_{0}^{s}g'(s-\tau)\left\|A^{\frac12}u(s)-A^{\frac12}u(\tau)\right\|^2d\tau\right)ds\notag\\
&=\int_{t}^{t+1}-E'(s)ds=E(t)-E(t+1):=[D(t)]^2.\label{nba}
\end{align}
By H\"older's inequality with \(\frac{\rho}{\rho+2}+\frac{2}{\rho+2}=1\),
\begin{align}\label{klll}
\int_{t}^{t+1}\|u_t(s)\|^{2}ds
&\leq\left(\int_{t}^{t+1}ds\right)^{\frac{\rho}{\rho+2}}\left(\int_{t}^{t+1}\|u_t(s)\|^{\rho+2}ds\right)^{\frac{2}{\rho+2}}
\leq[D(t)]^{\frac{4}{\rho+2}}.
\end{align}
By the mean value theorem, there exist \(t_1\in[t,t+\frac14]\) and \(t_2\in[t+\frac34,t+1]\) such that
\begin{align}
\|u_t(t_i)\|^2\leq4\int_{t}^{t+1}\|u_t(s)\|^{2}ds\leq4[D(t)]^{\frac{4}{\rho+2}},\qquad i=1,2.\label{mean}
\end{align}

Next, we consider the memory term. We have the decomposition
\begin{align}\label{cond1}
-\left(\int_{0}^{t}g(t-s)A^{\frac12}u(s)ds,A^{\frac12}u(t)\right)
&=\frac12\int_{0}^{t}g(t-s)\left\|A^{\frac12}u(t)-A^{\frac12}u(s)\right\|^2ds\notag\\
&\quad-\frac12\int_{0}^{t}g(s)ds\left\|A^{\frac12}u(t)\right\|^2\notag\\
&\quad-\frac12\int_{0}^{t}g(t-s)\left\|A^{\frac12}u(s)\right\|^2ds.
\end{align}
For the last term on the right-hand side of \eqref{cond1}, by (AG), \eqref{ed}, and \((a+b)^2\leq2a^2+2b^2\), we obtain
\begin{align}\label{cond2}
\frac12\int_{0}^{t}g(t-s)\left\|A^{\frac12}u(s)\right\|^2ds
&\leq-\frac{1}{2k}\int_{0}^{t}g'(t-s)\left\|A^{\frac12}u(s)\right\|^2ds\notag\\
&\leq-\frac{1}{k}\int_{0}^{t}g'(t-s)\left\|A^{\frac12}u(t)-A^{\frac12}u(s)\right\|^2ds\notag\\
&\quad+\frac{1}{k}\int_{0}^{t}-g'(t-s)ds\left\|A^{\frac12}u(t)\right\|^2\notag\\
&\leq\frac2k(-E'(t))+\frac{g(0)}{k}\left\|A^{\frac12}u(t)\right\|^2.
\end{align}
Multiplying \eqref{abstract} by \(u(t)\) and integrating over \(V_0\times(t_1,t_2)\), we get
\begin{align*}
\int_{t_1}^{t_2}\left(u_{ss}(s),u(s)\right)ds+\int_{t_1}^{t_2}\left[\left\|A^{\frac12}u(s)\right\|^2-\left(\int_{0}^{s}g(s-\tau)A^{\frac12}u(\tau)d\tau,A^{\frac12}u(s)\right)\right]ds\\
+\int_{t_1}^{t_2}\left(\|u_s(s)\|^{\rho}u_s(s),u(s)\right)ds=0.
\end{align*}
Since \(\frac{d}{dt}\left(u_{t}(t),u(t)\right)=\left(u_{tt}(t),u(t)\right)+\|u_t(t)\|^2\), this yields
\begin{align}
\int_{t_1}^{t_2}\left[\|A^{\frac12}u(s)\|^2-\left(\int_{0}^{s}g(s-\tau)A^{\frac12}u(\tau)d\tau,A^{\frac12}u(s)\right)\right]ds\notag\\
=\int_{t_1}^{t_2}\|u_s(s)\|^2ds+\sum\limits_{i=1}^{2}J_i,\label{key}
\end{align}
where
\[
J_1=(u(t_1),u_t(t_1))-(u(t_2),u_t(t_2)),\qquad
J_2=-\int_{t_1}^{t_2}\left(\|u_s(s)\|^{\rho}u_s(s),u(s)\right)ds.
\]
Replacing the second term on the left-hand side of \eqref{key} with \eqref{cond1}, we obtain
\begin{align*}
&\int_{t_1}^{t_2}\left(1-\frac12\int_{0}^{s}g(\tau)d\tau\right)\|A^{\frac12}u(s)\|^2ds+\frac12\int_{t_1}^{t_2}\int_{0}^{s}g(s-\tau)\|A^{\frac12}u(s)-A^{\frac12}u(\tau)\|^2d\tau ds\\
&\quad-\frac12\int_{t_1}^{t_2}\int_{0}^{s}g(s-\tau)\|A^{\frac12}u(\tau)\|^2d\tau ds=\int_{t_1}^{t_2}\|u_s(s)\|^2ds+\sum\limits_{i=1}^{2}J_i.
\end{align*}
Combining this with \eqref{cond2}, we get
\begin{align*}
&\int_{t_1}^{t_2}\left(1-\frac12\int_{0}^{s}g(\tau)d\tau-\frac{g(0)}{k}\right)\|A^{\frac12}u(s)\|^2ds\\
&\quad+\frac12\int_{t_1}^{t_2}\int_{0}^{s}g(s-\tau)\|A^{\frac12}u(s)-A^{\frac12}u(\tau)\|^2d\tau ds\\
&\leq\int_{t_1}^{t_2}\|u_s(s)\|^2ds+\sum\limits_{i=1}^{2}J_i+\frac2k\int_{t_1}^{t_2}(-E'(s))ds.
\end{align*}
Since \(k\geq2g(0)\), we have
\[
1-\frac12\int_0^sg(\tau)d\tau-\frac{g(0)}{k}\geq\frac12\left(1-\int_0^sg(\tau)d\tau\right).
\]
Thus, using \(E'(t)\leq0\), \(t_1\in[t,t+\frac14]\), and \(t_2\in[t+\frac34,t+1]\), we obtain
\begin{align*}
\int_{t_1}^{t_2}E(s)ds
&\leq\frac32\int_{t_1}^{t_2}\|u_s(s)\|^2ds+\sum\limits_{i=1}^{2}J_i+\frac2k\int_{t}^{t+1}(-E'(s))ds\\
&\leq\frac32\int_{t_1}^{t_2}\|u_s(s)\|^2ds+\sum\limits_{i=1}^{2}J_i+\frac2k[D(t)]^2,
\end{align*}
that is,
\begin{equation}\label{mid}
\int_{t_1}^{t_2}E(s)ds\leq\frac32\int_{t_1}^{t_2}\|u_s(s)\|^2ds+\sum\limits_{i=1}^{2}J_i+\frac2k[D(t)]^2.
\end{equation}

Since \(t\leq t_1<t_2\leq t+1\), by \eqref{klll},
\begin{equation}\label{klkl}
\int_{t_1}^{t_2}\|u_s(s)\|^2ds\leq\int_{t}^{t+1}\|u_s(s)\|^2ds\leq[D(t)]^{\frac{4}{\rho+2}}.
\end{equation}
Using \eqref{embed} with \(s_1=1\) and \(s_2=0\), we have \(\|u(t_i)\|\leq C_1\|A^{\frac12}u(t_i)\|\) with \(C_1:=\lambda_1^{-1/2}\). Hence, by \eqref{mu_0}, \eqref{energy}, and \(E(t)\geq E(t_i)\) for \(t_i\geq t\),
\[
\|u(t_i)\|\leq C_1\left\|A^{\frac12}u(t_i)\right\|\leq C_1\sqrt{\frac{2}{\mu_0}E(t_i)}\leq C_1\sqrt{\frac{2}{\mu_0}E(t)}.
\]
Together with \eqref{mean}, this gives
\[
J_1^2\leq2\left(\|u(t_1)\|^2\|u_t(t_1)\|^2+\|u(t_2)\|^2\|u_t(t_2)\|^2\right)\leq32C_1^2\mu_0^{-1}E(t)[D(t)]^{\frac{4}{\rho+2}},
\]
and hence, by Young's inequality,
\[
J_1\leq\epsilon E(t)+\frac{8C_1^2}{\epsilon\mu_0}[D(t)]^{\frac{4}{\rho+2}}
\]
for any \(\epsilon>0\).

By \eqref{energy} and \(E'(t)\leq0\), we have \(\|u_t\|^2\leq2E(0)\). Let \(C_2:=(2E(0))^{\frac{\rho}{2}}\). By H\"older's inequality, \eqref{klkl}, and Young's inequality, we obtain
\begin{align*}
J_2
&\leq C_2\int_{t_1}^{t_2}\|u(s)\|\|u_s(s)\|ds
\leq C_1C_2\int_{t_1}^{t_2}\|A^{\frac12}u(s)\|\|u_s(s)\|ds\\
&\leq C_1C_2\sqrt{2}\mu_0^{-\frac12}[E(t)]^{\frac12}\int_{t_1}^{t_2}\|u_s(s)\|ds
\leq C_1C_2\sqrt{2}\mu_0^{-\frac12}[E(t)]^{\frac12}\left(\int_{t_1}^{t_2}\|u_s(s)\|^2ds\right)^{\frac12}\\
&\leq C_1C_2\sqrt{2}\mu_0^{-\frac12}[E(t)]^{\frac12}[D(t)]^{\frac{2}{\rho+2}}
\leq\epsilon E(t)+\frac{C_1^2C_2^2}{2\epsilon\mu_0}[D(t)]^{\frac{4}{\rho+2}}
\end{align*}
for any \(\epsilon>0\).

Combining the estimates for \(J_1\) and \(J_2\) with \eqref{klkl} and \eqref{mid}, we get
\[
\int_{t_1}^{t_2}E(s)ds\leq2\epsilon E(t)+\left(\frac{8C_1^2}{\epsilon\mu_0}+\frac{C_1^2C_2^2}{2\epsilon\mu_0}+\frac32\right)[D(t)]^{\frac{4}{\rho+2}}+\frac2k[D(t)]^2.
\]
Since \([D(t)]^2\leq E(t)\) and \(E'(t)\leq0\), we have
\begin{equation}\label{lko}
[D(t)]^2=[D(t)]^{\frac{4}{\rho+2}}[D(t)]^{\frac{2\rho}{\rho+2}}\leq E(0)^{\frac{\rho}{\rho+2}}[D(t)]^{\frac{4}{\rho+2}}.
\end{equation}
Thus
\begin{equation}\label{next}
\int_{t_1}^{t_2}E(s)ds\leq2\epsilon E(t)+\mu_1[D(t)]^{\frac{4}{\rho+2}}
\end{equation}
for any \(\epsilon>0\), where
\[
\mu_1:=\frac{8C_1^2}{\epsilon\mu_0}+\frac{C_1^2C_2^2}{2\epsilon\mu_0}+\frac32+\frac2kE(0)^{\frac{\rho}{\rho+2}}.
\]
Since \(E'(t)\leq0\), the mean value theorem gives some \(\beta\in[t_1,t_2]\subset[t,t+1]\) such that
\begin{align}
\int_{t_1}^{t_2}E(s)ds=E(\beta)(t_2-t_1)\geq\frac12E(t+1).\label{most}
\end{align}
Combining \eqref{nba}, \eqref{next}, \eqref{most}, and \eqref{lko}, we obtain
\begin{align*}
E(t)
&=[D(t)]^2+E(t+1)\leq[D(t)]^2+2\int_{t_1}^{t_2}E(s)ds\\
&\leq[D(t)]^2+2\mu_1[D(t)]^{\frac{4}{\rho+2}}+4\epsilon E(t)\\
&\leq\left[E(0)^{\frac{\rho}{\rho+2}}+2\mu_1\right][D(t)]^{\frac{4}{\rho+2}}+4\epsilon E(t).
\end{align*}
Taking \(\epsilon=\frac18\), we get
\[
E(t)\leq2\left[E(0)^{\frac{\rho}{\rho+2}}+2\mu_1\right][D(t)]^{\frac{4}{\rho+2}},
\]
and hence
\[
[E(t)]^{1+\frac{\rho}{2}}\leq\mu[D(t)]^2=\mu[E(t)-E(t+1)],
\]
where
\[
\mu:=\left[2E(0)^{\frac{\rho}{\rho+2}}+4\mu_1\right]^{1+\frac{\rho}{2}}.
\]
Since \(E'(t)\leq0\),
\[
\sup_{t\leq s\leq t+1}[E(t)]^{1+\frac{\rho}{2}}\leq[E(t)]^{1+\frac{\rho}{2}}\leq\mu[E(t)-E(t+1)].
\]
Applying Lemma \ref{lemmp}, we obtain the desired decay estimates. This completes the proof for \(\rho\geq0\).
